hints: Focus on what gas is actually bubbled into the water when a Group 2 nitrate is heated strongly.
Recall that nitrogen dioxide dissolves in water to form acidic solutions of nitric and nitrous acids, so think what green universal indicator does in acid.
Compare Ca2+ and Sr2+ for polarising power to decide which nitrate is less thermally stable and so releases its acidic gas faster.
walkthrough:
**Write the thermal decomposition equation**

Group 2 nitrates decompose on heating to the oxide, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen. This is the gas mixture led into the water.

$$2\text{M}(\text{NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{MO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$$

**Decide the effect on universal indicator**

Oxygen has no effect on pH, but brown $\text{NO}_2$ dissolves to give an acidic solution.

$$2\text{NO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{HNO}_2 + \text{HNO}_3$$
Water with universal indicator starts neutral and green. Added $\text{H}^+$ turns it red, not blue, because the solution becomes acidic.

**Use the Group 2 stability trend for speed**

Thermal stability of nitrates increases down Group 2. A smaller cation like $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ polarises and distorts the large nitrate ion more than larger $\text{Sr}^{2+}$ does.
So $\text{Ca}(\text{NO}_3)_2$ decomposes more easily and produces $\text{NO}_2$ more quickly under identical heating. That gives green to red quickest for calcium nitrate.

options.A: Incorrect colour. Blue means alkaline, but the dissolved gas gives acid. Calcium nitrate is the faster nitrate, but green to blue is wrong.
options.B: Incorrect on both parts. The solution becomes acidic, not alkaline, so green to blue is wrong, and strontium nitrate is more stable and slower than calcium nitrate.
options.C: Correct. NO2 from decomposition forms HNO3 and HNO2 in water, turning neutral green indicator to acidic red. Ca(NO3)2 decomposes faster than Sr(NO3)2 because Ca2+ is smaller, more polarising and gives a less thermally stable nitrate.
options.D: Correct colour but wrong nitrate. Green to red is right for acidic NO2, but Sr(NO3)2 is more thermally stable down the group and reacts more slowly than Ca(NO3)2.
